subsubthemes.name: Designing and predicting proteins
subsubthemes.gist: Using AI to create new protein sequences and 3D shapes, either by learning from known structures or designing entirely new ones that fold correctly.

subsubthemes.name: Building molecules and drugs
subsubthemes.gist: Using AI to generate molecular structures and small drug-like compounds by understanding chemical space and constraints like synthesizability and binding properties.

subsubthemes.name: Simulating physical and biological systems
subsubthemes.gist: Using AI to model and predict how biological and chemical systems evolve over time, from protein dynamics to weather patterns and neural activity.

subsubthemes.name: Directing flow models and diffusion to build specific structures
subsubthemes.gist: Using flow matching and diffusion models with physics constraints and conditioning to guide the generation toward desired properties and realistic outputs.

subsubthemes.name: Optimizing designs through iteration and feedback
subsubthemes.gist: Using reinforcement learning, test-time scaling, and multi-objective optimization to iteratively improve designs based on desired properties like binding strength or stability.

subsubthemes.name: Combining sequence and structure with language
subsubthemes.gist: Using language models and multimodal learning to reason about biological sequences and structures as if they were text, enabling retrieval and design with textual queries.

subsubthemes.name: Extracting function from sparse biological data
subsubthemes.gist: Using diffusion and flow models to make sense of incomplete or noisy measurements from single cells, imaging, and other biological sensors to reveal hidden patterns.
